newsitem.title: USA: NY man charged in TWA victim credit card scam.
newsitem.headline: NY man charged in TWA victim credit card scam.

text.p: The friend of a woman killed on TWA Flight 800 in July was caught trying to open a Macy's department store account in the dead woman's name, officials said on Tuesday.

Police said Peter Santora, 50, was arrested and charged with grand larceny after presenting to the store eight credit cards belonging to crash victim Judith Yee and a doctored driver's license with her name and his photograph.

"He filled out an instant credit card application in her name and the associate that took the application obviously realised that something was not on the up and up," Macy's spokeswoman Ronnie Taffet said.
Santora, who lived next door to Yee in a posh Fifth Avenue apartment building in Manhattan, was questioned by security guards at the time of the incident on Sunday and they called the police.

All 230 passengers and crew were killed when the Boeing 747 exploded in mid-air without warning off New York's Long Island on July 17. Traces of explosives have been found on wreckage but investigators said they did not have enough evidence to conclude the plane was brought down by a bomb.
